evals.prompt: I'm a beginner looking at my Lambda CloudWatch logs and I see two different failures: Function A logs `REPORT RequestId: ... Duration: 10000.00 ms Billed Duration: 10000 ms Memory Size: 512 MB Max Memory Used: 95 MB Status: timeout` with zero logs after `START RequestId`, while Function B logs `Runtime.ExitError` with `Memory Size: 512 MB Max Memory Used: 512 MB`. What does each `REPORT` line mean, and how do I fix both functions?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-observability-and-triage skill, explains that Function A (`Duration >= Configured Timeout` with silence after `START RequestId` and low memory) indicates a network blackhole (such as a Lambda placed in a private VPC subnet without a NAT Gateway or VPC Endpoint) or missing SDK `connect_timeout`/`read_timeout`, while Function B (`Max Memory Used == Memory Size` + `Runtime.ExitError`) indicates an Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crash (remediated by streaming S3 files instead of buffering in RAM/global caches and/or increasing `MemorySize`).
expectations: Activates the serverless-observability-and-triage skill and diagnoses Function A (`Status: timeout` at the exact configured limit with silence after `START RequestId`) as a VPC network blackhole or missing SDK client `connect_timeout`/`read_timeout`

Diagnoses Function B (`Max Memory Used == Memory Size` with `Runtime.ExitError`) as an Out-of-Memory (OOM) crash and recommends checking for unbounded global caches or large in-memory buffers before increasing `MemorySize`
Shows setting explicit `botocore.config.Config(connect_timeout=2, read_timeout=5, retries={'max_attempts': 2})` shorter than the Lambda function timeout

evals.prompt: I am new to AWS and my React frontend calling an API Gateway + Lambda backend is failing with three errors: (1) `502 Bad Gateway` with `Execution failed due to configuration error: Malformed Lambda proxy response` when my handler returns `return {"user": "alice"}`, (2) `504 Gateway Timeout` when generating a large PDF takes 35 seconds, and (3) browser CORS errors (`No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header`) whenever the API returns a `401` or `500` error even though `200 OK` works fine. How do I fix all three?
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-observability-and-triage skill and explains: (1) `AWS_PROXY` requires returning the proxy envelope `{"statusCode": 200, "headers": {...}, "body": json.dumps(data), "isBase64Encoded": False}` where `body` is a JSON-serialized string, (2) API Gateway enforces a 29-second default integration timeout (`504`), so work taking 35s should either be optimized, moved to an async `202 Accepted` + SQS/Step Functions polling pattern, or served via a Lambda Function URL with `RESPONSE_STREAM`, and (3) CORS headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`) must be returned on both `2xx` and `4xx/5xx` Lambda proxy responses AND configured on API Gateway `GatewayResponses` (`DEFAULT_4XX`, `DEFAULT_5XX`) when authorizers or throttles reject requests before Lambda runs.
expectations: Activates the serverless-observability-and-triage skill and shows the required `AWS_PROXY` response format (`statusCode`, `headers`, stringified `body`, `isBase64Encoded`) to resolve the 502 Malformed Lambda proxy response error

Explains that 504 Gateway Timeout occurs because API Gateway's default integration timeout is 29 seconds, and recommends async `202 Accepted` processing (or Function URL `RESPONSE_STREAM` / timeout tuning)

Explains that fixing CORS on `4xx/5xx` requires both returning `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` in error branches of the Lambda handler AND configuring API Gateway `GatewayResponses` (`DEFAULT_4XX`, `DEFAULT_5XX`)

expectations: Activates the serverless-observability-and-triage skill and explains Step Functions Redrive (`redrive-execution` and `redrive-map-run`) to resume Standard Workflows and Distributed Map runs from the point of failure without re-running completed steps

evals.prompt: A FinOps tool flagged three single-threaded Node.js/Python Lambda functions in ap-south-1 because all three show `memUtilizationPct = 20%`: Function 1 (`1024 MB`, waits 400ms on DynamoDB and external REST APIs), Function 2 (`1024 MB`, spends 400ms doing heavy cryptographic SHA-256 hashing and JSON parsing in CPU), and Function 3 (`3008 MB`, single-threaded Node.js event loop doing CPU work). Should we blindly drop `MemorySize` by 75% on all three? Explain the exact vCPU-to-memory thresholds and what happens to cost and latency on each.
evals.expected_output: Activates the serverless-observability-and-triage skill, states the exact Lambda vCPU scaling thresholds (**1,769 MB = 1 full vCPU**, **3,538 MB = 2 vCPUs**), and differentiates the three functions: (1) Function 1 is **I/O-bound** (CPU is idle waiting on sockets, so lowering from `1024 MB` to `256 MB` barely changes `@duration` and cuts GB-second cost by up to 75%), (2) Function 2 is **CPU-bound** (halving memory halves fractional vCPU, which doubles `@duration`—yielding `0.5x memory * 2x duration = 1.0x` identical cost with 2x worse latency; increasing to `1769 MB` can halve duration at ~0 net cost change), and (3) Function 3 (`3008 MB` single-threaded) cannot use the second vCPU core above `1,769 MB`, so it should be right-sized to `1,769 MB` and migrated to `arm64` (up to 34% better price-performance).
expectations: Activates the serverless-observability-and-triage skill and cites the exact Lambda vCPU scaling boundaries (`1,769 MB = 1 full vCPU` and `3,538 MB = 2 vCPUs`)
Contrasts I/O-bound Function 1 (safe to lower memory for up to 75% GB-s savings) against CPU-bound Function 2 (where halving memory doubles duration, keeping GB-s cost flat while doubling latency)

Explains why single-threaded Function 3 at `3,008 MB` wastes all memory/CPU allocation above `1,769 MB` because a single-threaded event loop cannot utilize a second vCPU core, and recommends capping at `1,769 MB` on `arm64`
